headline: A daughter saves her dad's shoe shop

sources.title: Daughter Saves Dad's Struggling Shoe Shop With TikTok Appeal
Watch: viral TikToks save Shoreditch's last shoe shop
Hidden gem shoe shop goes viral thanks to supporters, now with long queues
Viral TikToks saves Shoreditch's last shoe shop (video, Roxy)

chunks.text: For more than twenty years, Rachid Lazraq has {{looked after}} a small shoe shop called Rich Collection Italia on Hackney Road in East London. The shop sells [[stylish]] Italian shoes, but [[in recent years]] [[business]] had slowly {{dried up}}. Most people had started buying online, and [[fewer and fewer]] [[customers]] [[came through the door]]. Sad and tired, Rachid had almost decided to {{shut down}} the shop [[for good]].

verbs.why: Parents look after young children, and neighbors look after each other's pets on vacation. For more than twenty years, Rachid looked after his small shoe shop in East London.

verbs.wrong: To lose money on every sale
verbs.why: A river can dry up in a drought, and interest in an old hobby can dry up over time. At the shoe shop, business slowly dried up as more customers began shopping online.

verbs.correct: To close a business for good
verbs.wrong: To sell the shop to someone
verbs.why: Owners shut down struggling stores, and towns sometimes shut down factories that lose too much money. Rachid had almost decided to shut down his shoe shop for good.

chunks.text: His daughter, who is 25 and works as a [[journalist]], did not want to {{give up}} on the [[family business]]. She had {{found out}} that a French [[influencer]] had shown the shop online, so she {{came up with}} a simple idea. On July 7, she posted a short [[video]] on TikTok about the shop's Y2K [[sandals]], a [[style]] from the early 2000s that is [[popular]] again.

verbs.wrong: To lose all of your money
verbs.why: People give up smoking, give up bad habits, and sometimes give up on a dream too soon. His daughter refused to give up on the family business without a fight.

verbs.correct: To learn a fact or the truth
verbs.why: Reporters find out secrets through sources, and shoppers find out about sales through friends. She found out that a French influencer had already shown the shop online.

verbs.correct: To think of a new idea
verbs.why: Students come up with excuses, and inventors come up with clever new ideas. His daughter came up with a simple idea: post a video about the shop's sandals.

chunks.text: The video quickly {{took off}}. [[Overnight]], it {{racked up}} 300,000 [[views]], and soon young customers were {{lining up}} outside the shop, sometimes waiting two hours to get inside. [[In just a few days]], the whole business had {{turned around}}. The quiet little shop that was about to close was suddenly [[full of life]].

verbs.wrong: To be posted early in the morning
verbs.why: A new song can take off in just one week, and a small business idea can take off after one good review. The daughter's TikTok video quickly took off, reaching hundreds of thousands of viewers.
Shoppers rack up credit card debt, and gamers rack up points during a long match. Overnight, the daughter's video racked up 300,000 views and brought a wave of new customers.

verbs.correct: To form a line and wait
verbs.why: Fans line up for concert tickets, and shoppers line up outside stores before a big sale. Young customers began lining up outside the shop, sometimes waiting two hours to get in.

verbs.correct: To change from bad to good
verbs.wrong: To move a shop somewhere new
verbs.why: A new coach can turn around a losing team, and a good plan can turn around a failing business. In just a few days, the whole shop had turned around and was full of life again.

chunks.text: The best moment came when Rachid {{took down}} the 'Closing Sale' [[sign]] while happy customers {{cheered him on}}. His daughter, who had hated to watch the shop [[struggle]], could [[hardly]] believe how quickly things had changed. Now the family is even {{looking into}} selling their Italian shoes online. One short video had {{brought back}} the [[crowds]] and given a [[much loved]] little shop a [[second chance]].

verbs.correct: To remove something from its place
verbs.wrong: To lower the prices in a shop
verbs.why: Workers take down old posters, and campers take down their tents before leaving. Rachid finally took down the old 'Closing Sale' sign from the shop window.
Fans cheer on their team, and parents cheer on their kids at a race. Happy customers cheered Rachid on as he removed the shop's old closing sign.
Managers look into complaints, and travelers look into cheap flights before booking. The family is now looking into selling their Italian shoes online as well.

verbs.wrong: To welcome people into a shop
verbs.why: A song can bring back old memories, and a store can bring back a popular item. One short video had brought back the crowds and given this small shop a second chance.

mainIdea.s: A daughter's TikTok video about her father's small shoe shop suddenly took off online. The shop, which was about to shut down for good, is now full of customers and looking into selling online.
mainIdea.why: His daughter posted a video about the shop's Y2K sandals, and it racked up 300,000 views overnight. Customers then lined up outside, and the family is now looking into selling shoes online.

mainIdea.s: Worried her father's shop would close, a woman asked a well-known online influencer to post a video about the sandals herself. The video went viral, and customers soon lined up outside the shop.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the daughter posted the video herself, not the influencer. The influencer had only shown the shop online earlier, before the daughter's own post went viral.

mainIdea.s: A small bakery in East London announced this month that it would close for good after many years of falling sales. The owner said online orders could not make up for the drop in customers.
mainIdea.why: This is about a different shop that is closing, not one that TikTok saved. The real story is about the shop owner's shoe shop, which his daughter saved with a viral video.
